faq: Do I need consent to follow up?
Yes. We only follow up with people who gave their email and agreed to hear from you. The chat includes a clear consent line, and every email has an unsubscribe link.
Can the follow up use what the shopper asked?
Yes, in a light way, such as We saw you asked about sizing. It uses the topic, not a full chat transcript, which keeps messages helpful and avoids sounding intrusive.
Will it keep emailing after a purchase?
No. The flow stops when an order appears for that email address, or when the person unsubscribes. We test this with sample orders before launch.
How is this different from abandoned cart emails?
Cart emails target people who added items. These follow up on a chat question, even when the cart was empty. Both can run together, with rules that stop messages from doubling up.

desc:
Follow up messages for shoppers with questions are polite emails sent after a chat, with consent, that remember what the person asked. Ecom Swift LLC writes the emails, sets the timing and connects them to your email tool, with your approval before anything goes out.

## What are chat follow up messages?

Chat follow up messages are short emails sent to a shopper who asked a question in your chat, left, and agreed to hear from you. The email refers to the question, gives a helpful answer or link and invites the shopper back to the product.

They differ from a standard abandoned cart email. A cart email reacts to items left in a basket. A chat follow up reacts to a doubt the shopper spoke aloud, which is usually a clearer sign of interest.

## Why a shopper's question deserves a reply later

A question is a signal. Someone asking whether a jacket runs small or whether a part fits an older model is close to a decision and missing one piece of information. If the answer was given in chat and the person left anyway, a gentle reminder a day later can arrive when they are ready to return.

Done badly, follow up feels like pursuit. Done well, it feels like service: the store remembered what you wanted to know. The difference lies in consent, timing, tone and stopping at the right moment.

## How follow up affects returning visitors and orders

The mechanism is relevance. A message that mentions the exact topic gets read more willingly than a generic promotion because it continues a conversation the shopper started. A link that lands on the product they asked about saves them searching again.

Stop rules protect the relationship. The sequence ends when the person buys, replies or unsubscribes, so nobody receives an offer for something they already own. Results vary with the product, the price and the quality of the answer, and we do not promise a specific outcome. We build the flow so it is polite, accurate and easy to measure.

## What a good follow up flow includes

- Consent captured clearly before any email is sent.
- A first email that mentions the topic of the chat in plain words.
- A link straight back to the product or page discussed.
- A second email with a different angle, such as sizing or delivery information.
- Timing that fits the topic, for example one day and a few days later.
- Stop rules for purchase, reply and unsubscribe.
- An approval step so a person on your team reviews wording.
- Subject lines you can test against each other.
- Quiet hours based on the shopper's time zone.
- Checks for bounces and unsubscribes.

## How we set it up

We read your chat topics and choose the questions that most often come before a purchase, such as sizing, shipping or compatibility. For each, we write a short email in your voice and agree the timing with you.

Then we connect the chat to your email tool, make sure consent is recorded and test the whole sequence with sample conversations, including a shopper who buys halfway through and one who unsubscribes. Basic delivers one email. Standard adds a three step flow, timing, chat topic in the message and an approval step. Premium adds flows by topic, subject variations, quiet hours and bounce checks.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Contact only the leads who said yes to receiving your messages.
- Reference the question in a helpful, not pushy, way.
- Put the unsubscribe option in every email.
- Review the first sends by hand before the flow runs freely.
- Keep each email short, with a single clear link.

**Avoid:**
- Emailing shoppers who never gave consent.
- Quoting private details from the chat that the shopper may not expect to see.
- Continuing the sequence after a purchase.
- Sending at night in the shopper's time zone.
- Adding a discount to every message, which trains people to wait.

## Who this is for

This fits a store whose chat sees many pre purchase questions and loses some of those shoppers afterwards. It suits sellers of products that need reassurance, such as clothing, equipment, supplements or anything with options. It also suits a small team that wants a consistent follow up without writing each email by hand.

## What we need from you

Send examples of your brand voice, your email tool name, your consent wording and the questions you hear most. Tell us who will approve email text.

We work in your own accounts, never need passwords and are given access as a collaborator, staff or team user where the platform supports it. You can remove access at any time. We send a checklist after you order and show you each email before it is switched on.
